card.name: Comma ending an opening if-clause
card.fires_on: The comma (occasionally the next word) that closes a conditional or concessive opening clause, such as 'If X ...,' or 'However X might have been,', just before the main clause begins.

modes.label: Comma after if-clause
modes.description: The comma closing an 'if' clause, right before the main clause.

modes.label: Comma after concessive clause
modes.description: The comma after a clause starting with 'However' or similar, before the main statement.

modes.label: Word after clause break
modes.description: A word starting the main clause when no comma is present.
modes.example: If a time traveler from a hundred years ago were to visit a home today,<< much>> of the technology would be completely alien.
